what: A stack of overlapping pieces (lids and bodies) inside a pinned panel spreads open from the lower pieces as you scroll — the top lid stays in place, the rest move down by (i+1)×gap, each .06 later, over a .82 length power3.inOut. The gap is measured by dividing the leftover height in the panel by the number of pieces. It does not follow progress directly: opening trails with power2.out over max(.35s, distance÷1), while closing uses .6s expo.out and finishes closing by itself when within 30% of closed (magnet). The cover value (total price) lifts away from .05 over a .3 length, and the side values and buttons float up from .6 over a .4 length. After fully open it holds for 1.15 before moving on to the next

options.group: Opens and closes together using the progress of the cell scrolled furthest among cells with the same name (side-by-side stacks). If none, each cell works on its own
options.snap: If on, snaps a resting spot in the inner scroll panel to the nearest state (closed · open) — only in the direction of travel. In a group, only one is snapped
options.hold: Hold time while fully open (as a share of open spread 1), default 1.15
options.run: Length over which one piece spreads out, default .82
options.lag: Opening page follow-through minimum seconds, default .35
options.rate: Max speed of the opening page (progress per second), default 1
options.magnet: Magnet range on the closing side (share of the opening), default .3
options.open: Screens covered by Spread 1 in the inner scroll panel, default .714 — wall height = (1 + open × (1 + hold)) × panel height
options.travel: Number of screens of scrolling needed for the window to open by 1, default 1.54
options.clear: Gap (px) between the last unfolded piece and the panel’s bottom edge, default 40
options.wall: In the css mode inside a scroll panel, the part does not set the wall height and leaves it to the consumer’s CSS — height: calc((1 + open × (1 + hold)) × panel height expression). When the panel height changes via a variable, the wall follows in the same frame
options.--fx-top: Height where the panel sticks (below header row), default 0

— Values and buttons beside the piece use data-fx-part="side". When closed/open changes, the element gets data-state and fx:state(detail.open)
note: The pieces keep the flow layout, overlapped with negative margins, and move down by transform only (the flow is unchanged, so the cover spots stay the same). In window scroll, if the panel is shorter than the screen, the panel and wall are enlarged. At the wall’s tail end the panel is pulled up by half the placement distance with power2.in to match the speed at landing to the scroll, and the next section is pulled in by that amount. The original also capped wheel input at 100px per tick and a lead of .3 screens. That is Lenis-side work, so it lives in the site’s shared.js
